title: Gallstones and Acute Cholecystitis
summary: Separate colic from cholecystitis, climb the investigation ladder, grade with TG18 and choose the right operation and timing.
closing: Stone alone is not the indication: symptoms, grade and fitness decide, and the duct and the critical view decide safety.

objectives.text: Tell biliary colic from acute cholecystitis using pain duration, fever and tenderness, and pick the cause of cholecystitis
Choose the most common gallstone type as the exam key expects, and say what current texts say instead
Match each pigment stone type to its site and associations, and name the risk factors of cholesterol stones
Pick the first test and the most sensitive and specific test for gallstones and acute cholecystitis
Choose MRCP over ultrasound, CT or diagnostic ERCP when CBD stones are suspected
Build the TG18 suspected versus definite diagnosis from A, B and C
Assign TG18 grade I, II or III from the stated cut-offs
Choose treatment by TG18 grade, fitness and calculous or acalculous type: early surgery, drainage or delayed
Decide who needs cholecystectomy, dissolution therapy or nothing among stone patients
Tell Mirizzi, gallstone ileus, Bouveret, cholangitis and emphysematous cholecystitis apart, and name gallstone pancreatitis
Apply Courvoisier's law only to a jaundiced patient with a non-tender palpable gallbladder
Confirm the critical view of safety and name the commonest cause of bile duct injury before clipping

traps.trap: Most common gallstone type is cholesterol, not mixed as the PYQ key expects
Ultrasound is the answer to 'most sensitive and specific' for acute cholecystitis; CT as initial test
Ultrasound, CT or diagnostic ERCP chosen for CBD stones instead of MRCP
Biliary colic is truly colicky, so day-long pain with fever is still biliary colic
Courvoisier's law applies to any palpable gallbladder, so it always means malignancy
TG18 suspected versus definite diagnosis set built wrongly (A+B vs A+B+C)
TG18 grading numbers swapped with familiar sepsis or lab cut-offs
Early laparoscopic cholecystectomy is the answer in every TG18 grade
Interval cholecystectomy at 6-8 weeks (older key) chosen over early surgery
Asymptomatic gallstones should be removed because stones are a risk
Ursodeoxycholic acid dissolves any stone
Black and brown pigment stone associations swapped
Bouveret's syndrome and gallstone ileus swapped as to site
Charcot's triad and Reynolds' pentad blurred
Emphysematous cholecystitis is caused by E. coli, as in any infected gallbladder
Seeing two structures is enough for the critical view of safety
Commonest cause of major bile duct injury is vascular or bleeding
Mirizzi syndrome is a stone in the CBD rather than external compression
Acalculous cholecystitis is milder than calculous because no stone obstructs
Acalculous cholecystitis in a critically ill patient treated by early cholecystectomy
